## 1. Large deviations

### A fair coin tossed 10 times
```{r fair-coin}
p <- 0.5
n <- 10
x <- 0:n 
expected <- n*p
for(d in 0:max(expected,n-expected)){
  deviated <- abs(x-expected)>=d
  barplot(dbinom(x,n,p),col=c("blue","red")[deviated+1],border=NA,
          main=paste("Probability of deviating by",d,"or more is",sum(dbinom(x[deviated],n,p))),
          names.arg=0:n)
}  
```   


### A biased coin with $p=0.2$ tossed 10 times, "symmetric" deviations

```{r biased-coin-symm}
p <- 0.2
n <- 10
x <- 0:n 
expected <- n*p
for(d in 0:max(expected,n-expected)){
  deviated <- abs(x-expected)>=d
  barplot(dbinom(x,n,p),col=c("blue","red")[deviated+1],border=NA,
          main=paste("Probability of deviating by",d,"or more is",sum(dbinom(x[deviated],n,p))),
          names.arg=0:n)
}  
```   


### A biased coin with $p=0.2$ tossed 10 times, "equally spread" deviations 

```{r biased-coin-equal}
p <- 0.2
n <- 10
x <- 0:n 
expected <- n*p
for(lower.bound in 0:(expected-1)){
  lower.deviated <- 0:lower.bound
  lower.probability <- sum(dbinom(lower.deviated,n,p))
  upper.bound <- qbinom(lower.probability,n,p,lower.tail=FALSE)
  upper.deviated <- upper.bound:n
  deviated <- rep.int(FALSE,n+1)
  deviated[c(lower.deviated,upper.deviated)+1] <- TRUE
  barplot(dbinom(x,n,p),col=c("blue","red")[deviated+1],border=NA,
          main=paste("Probability of deviating up to",lower.bound,
                    "and the other side is",sum(dbinom(x[deviated],n,p))),
          names.arg=0:n)
} 
for(upper.bound in (expected+1):n){
  upper.deviated <- upper.bound:n
  upper.probability <- sum(dbinom(upper.deviated,n,p))
  lower.bound <- qbinom(upper.probability,n,p)
  lower.deviated <- 0:lower.bound
  deviated <- rep.int(FALSE,n+1)
  deviated[c(lower.deviated,upper.deviated)+1] <- TRUE
  barplot(dbinom(x,n,p),col=c("blue","red")[deviated+1],border=NA,
          main=paste("Probability of deviating from",upper.bound,
                    "and the other side is",sum(dbinom(x[deviated],n,p))),
          names.arg=0:n)
}
```   


## 2. Hypothesis testing

We will be testing the hypothesis $p=0.5$.
```{r}
p.hypothesised <- 0.5
```   

### Analytic procedure

Let's see what happens when the hypothesis is actually false.
```{r}
n <- 10
p <- 0.2
```   

Let's generate a sample from the actual distribution $p=`r p`$:
```{r}
x <- rbinom(1,n,p)
x
```   

Now calculate the probability of a deviation at least as large as in the sample
for samples from the hypothesised distribution:
```{r p-value-analytic}
(expected <- n*p.hypothesised)
(deviation <- abs(x-expected))
lower.bound <- expected - deviation
upper.bound <- expected + deviation
upper.bound <- ifelse((upper.bound-floor(upper.bound)) < .Machine$double.eps,upper.bound-1,floor(upper.bound))
pbinom(lower.bound,n,p.hypothesised) + 1 - pbinom(upper.bound,n,p.hypothesised)
```   

The probability ($p$-value) is not small, so we cannot reject the hypothesis.

### Simulated procedure

We will use the same sample from the actual distribution with $p=`r p`$ as above.
```{r}
x
```   

Now let's generate many samples from the hypothesised distribution
```{r p-value-simulation}
num.simulations <- 1e6
simulated.X <- rbinom(num.simulations,n,p.hypothesised)
```   
and compare the deviations:
```{r p-value-simulation-comparison}
expected <- n*p.hypothesised
mean(abs(simulated.X - expected)>=abs(x-expected))
```   


## 3. Confidence Sets

The function below returns True if the hypothesis is rejected and False otherwise.
```{r function-test-hyp}
test.hypothesis <- function(significance.level,sample.size,x.sample,probability.hypothesised){
  expected <- sample.size*probability.hypothesised;
  deviation <- abs(x.sample-expected);
  lower.bound <- expected - deviation;
  upper.bound <- expected + deviation;
  upper.bound <- ifelse( (upper.bound-floor(upper.bound)) < .Machine$double.eps, 
                         upper.bound - 1,floor(upper.bound))
  p.value <- 
    pbinom(lower.bound,sample.size,probability.hypothesised) + 
    1 - pbinom(upper.bound,sample.size,probability.hypothesised);
  return(p.value < significance.level);
}
```  

Let's fix some significance level:
```{r}
alpha <- 0.05
```   

Now let's test several hypotheses at once. We begin with values of $p=0,0.1,0.2,\ldots,1$ and print those
that are not rejected:
```{r conf-set-01}
possible.hypotheses <- seq(from=0,to=1,by=0.1);
rejected.hypotheses <- sapply(possible.hypotheses,function(p.h){test.hypothesis(alpha,n,x,p.h)})
possible.hypotheses[!rejected.hypotheses]
```    

Let's print those values as an interval:
```{r}
interval <- function(vector){c(min(vector),max(vector))}
interval(possible.hypotheses[!rejected.hypotheses])
```   

Now a finer set of hypotheses, every $0.01$, and the non-rejected are plotted in blue:
```{r conf-set-001}
possible.hypotheses <- seq(from=0,to=1,by=0.01);
rejected.hypotheses <- sapply(possible.hypotheses,function(p.h){test.hypothesis(alpha,n,x,p.h)})
plot(x=possible.hypotheses,y=rep_len(1,length(rejected.hypotheses)),col=c("blue","red")[rejected.hypotheses+1],
     pch=19,ylab="")
interval(possible.hypotheses[!rejected.hypotheses])
```    

And an even finer set, every $0.001$:
```{r conf-set-0001,fig.width=12}
possible.hypotheses <- seq(from=0,to=1,by=0.001);
rejected.hypotheses <- sapply(possible.hypotheses,function(p.h){test.hypothesis(alpha,n,x,p.h)})
plot(x=possible.hypotheses,y=rep_len(1,length(rejected.hypotheses)),col=c("blue","red")[rejected.hypotheses+1],
     pch=".",ylab="")
interval(possible.hypotheses[!rejected.hypotheses])
```    

And now every $0.0001$:
```{r conf-set-00001,fig.width=12}
possible.hypotheses <- seq(from=0,to=1,by=0.0001);
rejected.hypotheses <- sapply(possible.hypotheses,function(p.h){test.hypothesis(alpha,n,x,p.h)})
plot(x=possible.hypotheses,y=rep_len(1,length(rejected.hypotheses)),col=c("blue","red")[rejected.hypotheses+1],
     pch=".",ylab="")
interval(possible.hypotheses[!rejected.hypotheses])
```
